skip_reason: Not a sales call. Inbound post-move service-recovery and damage complaint from a customer (Mohammad Khan) whose move the Dallas team completed the prior day. Grant is the Fort Worth manager, confirmed the move was not his branch, and spent the entire call taking the complaint and arranging a callback from the Dallas branch manager. No quote, no pricing, no booking, no estimate content — nothing on the sales scorecard applies.
top_strength: Grant took a hostile situation without a shred of defensiveness. When the customer offered to leave the damage uncleaned so someone could inspect it, Grant said "No, that's okay. We won't, we trust it... We trust you" — which de-escalated instantly. He also told the customer to be blunt with the Dallas manager: "I wouldn't be afraid to just tell him exactly what she told me," and framed the complaint as useful: "that's the only way that we get better and we keep things from like this, from happening to other people."
coaching_note: Not gradeable as a sales call, but three live business risks in this transcript need escalation today, and one process gap is Grant's own. LIVE RISK 1 — a Dallas mover called this customer roughly an hour after the move asking "where's the other half of the tip," after earlier telling him on-site "I told we would get those $300 a piece" and pressuring for a tip on a claimed three-hour time savings the customer says never existed. That is a solicitation-and-harassment issue, not a service issue, and the customer explicitly says he has the call log and is weighing taking it "to a higher level." LIVE RISK 2 — significant unreported damage: scratched doors, chipped paint, broken furniture, and blood on two walls, plus sweat/body odor on an uncovered mattress because the crew reportedly had no mattress covers. The apartment complex ran a pre- and post-move inspection and is billing the damage back to the customer. LIVE RISK 3 — no damage claim was opened. Grant asked directly ("did we do a damage claim with you at all yesterday") and the answer was "Nothing" — one mover said "I'm sorry, I'll take care of it" and nothing was filed. Grant's own gap: he correctly routed to the Dallas branch manager but did not open a claim himself, so the only thing protecting this customer right now is a promised callback with no ETA. Someone should file the claim and reach out proactively rather than waiting on the branch handoff. The customer's structural suggestion is also worth hearing: movers should not hold customer phone numbers directly, and communication should route through the front office.
phone_presence_notes: Genuinely warm and non-defensive under a heated complaint — validated repeatedly ("Yeah, absolutely", "we trust you", "that's gross"), invited full candor with the Dallas manager, and the customer ended appreciative ("I sincerely appreciate it", "Take care"), though he never used the customer's name correctly and the call was disrupted by his own connection drop.
audio_review_reason: Mid-call internet drop ("I lost a little bit internet connection there and I had to set up my Ethernet real fast") plus several out-of-order and garbled lines leave real gaps in what Grant actually said and committed to. Audio should be pulled anyway to preserve evidence of the tip-solicitation complaint before it escalates.
